passage:
Thursday
Today scared me. After PE, Dhruv was sitting on the changing-room bench, gasping and shaking, saying, "I can't breathe, I can't breathe." For a second I thought something terrible was happening to his heart, and my own hands went cold. I didn't know what to do, so I did what our coach once told us. I sat next to him, not too close, and talked slowly. "I'm here. You're breathing. Try breathing out long, like me." I asked the others to wait outside so it was quieter, and sent Anu to get Coach in case he needed a doctor. By the time Coach came, Dhruv's breathing was slower. Coach stayed with him and called his parents. Tonight he texted me: "Thanks for not leaving." I'm still shaky.
Kalyani

qa.q: Where was Dhruv sitting after PE?
qa.a: Dhruv was sitting on the changing-room bench.

qa.q: What was Kalyani feeling when Dhruv said he couldn't breathe?
qa.a: Kalyani was frightened, fearing something terrible was happening to Dhruv's heart, and felt cold hands.

qa.q: Which of Kalyani's actions helped, and why?
qa.a: Staying near, talking slowly, clearing the room so it was quieter and sending for Coach in case a doctor was needed all kept Dhruv calmer and safer.

qa.q: What might Dhruv have felt when he texted "Thanks for not leaving"?
qa.a: Dhruv likely felt grateful and relieved that someone stayed beside him while he felt he could not breathe.

grounding: A friend sees someone gasping and shaking, fears something terrible is happening, and helps by staying near, speaking slowly, keeping it quiet and calling an adult.
